description:
Team interested in exploring different ideas involving GIS, aerospace, remote sensing, and engineering. currently working on a few projects involving drones, aerial mapping, and surveying, and I figured this would be a good opportunity to experiment with something new.

For this challenge, I'm hoping to learn more about satellite radar imagery, test a few ideas, and see how I could apply what I learn to some of my existing projects. Nothing too fancy, just experimenting, and learning.
summary:
NeoGeo is an environmental monitoring platform that uses Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) satellite imagery to detect, measure, and visualize geographic changes over time. By comparing observations from different dates, NeoGeo identifies changes in radar backscatter that may indicate shifts in waterways, coastlines, wetlands, and surrounding landscapes.

The platform combines change detection, noise filtering, uncertainty analysis, and interactive geographic mapping to highlight changes while accounting for potential measurement errors.

We tested NeoGeo using Sentinel-1 imagery of Jacksonville, Florida, and NASA's NISAR sample datasets. Our tests demonstrated successful radar data processing, geographic change analysis, and zero detected change when comparing identical inputs.

NeoGeo aims to provide a practical way to monitor environmental changes, measure their geographic extent, and support further scientific analysis using satellite radar observations.
details:
NeoGeo — Project Details

NeoGeo started with a simple idea: what if we could use satellite radar to see how our environment changes over time, even when those changes aren't immediately visible?

For this project, I built an application that compares SAR satellite images taken on different dates and highlights differences across the landscape. I first tested it using Sentinel-1 imagery of Jacksonville, Florida, looking at changes around waterways, coastlines, and surrounding land.

One of the biggest challenges was figuring out which differences were meaningful and which could simply be radar noise. To help with this, I added filtering, adjustable detection thresholds, and error analysis. NeoGeo also creates color-coded change maps, estimates how much area is affected, and shows the results on an interactive geographic map.

I also wanted the project to work with NASA's NISAR mission, so I added support for its GCOV radar datasets. I tested the application using NASA's sample files from two different dates and ran an additional test comparing the same file against itself. As expected, the identical images produced no detected changes.

NeoGeo is still a work in progress. A change in radar measurements doesn't always mean the environment itself has changed, so further testing and independent observations are important.

My goal is to keep developing NeoGeo into a tool that can help track changes in rivers, wetlands, coastlines, and other environments, while making sure the results are useful, measurable, and scientifically responsible.
